findings.evidence: This reset link expired an hour after it was sent... Container: toast. Fires: on-focus. The reader cannot complete the password reset without requesting a new link.
findings.fix: Use a modal dialog that persists until the reader dismisses it or takes the suggested action (request new link), rather than a self-clearing toast.
findings.violation: A blocking failure (expired reset link prevents form completion) is presented in a self-clearing toast container, so a reader who looks away misses the only message explaining why they cannot proceed.

findings.evidence: Please correct the highlighted field. Error code: 502. Placement: directly below the shipping address block, but text says only 'the highlighted field'.
findings.fix: Name the specific field and the actual problem: for example, 'The shipping address entry failed (error 502). Please re-enter the address and save again.'
findings.violation: The message names neither the field nor the underlying problem; it relies entirely on visual highlighting to identify which field is wrong, leaving a non-sighted or colorblind reader with only a generic reference and an internal error code.

findings.evidence: Please correct the highlighted field. Error code: 502.
findings.fix: Replace the code or jargon term with a plain-language sentence a non-technical reader can act on.
findings.violation: The message text carries an internal error code, a code-style token, or an engineering-jargon term standing in for a plain-language explanation.

findings.evidence: Receipts upload as PDF or PNG only... Fires: on-submit. File type validation is a format check the product already knows at file-selection time.
findings.fix: Show a format requirement message or pre-filter file selection when the user picks a file, before form submission.
findings.violation: The message reports a predictable mistake detected at submission, but the product could plausibly have warned about the file type requirement during file selection, before the reader committed the wrong format.

findings.evidence: Placement: at the top of a long form, requiring the reader to scroll up to see it, though the field itself stays visible on the page.
findings.fix: Position the message directly below the password field it concerns, on the same visible area without requiring scrolling.
findings.violation: The message appears at the top of a long form, requiring the reader to scroll away from the field to see it, even though both are on the same screen.

findings.evidence: This receipt is over the 10 MB limit... Reduce the file size and upload it again. Suggested fix: described, names the one available alternative but requires the reader to enter it by hand.
findings.fix: Offer a selectable action to compress the file automatically or let the reader choose a compression level, rather than only describing the fix in text.
findings.violation: The message names a single, unambiguous fix (reduce file size) but only describes it in prose, requiring the reader to manually reduce the file outside the product and re-upload, rather than offering a selectable compress action.
